root_cause.text: The DAMON core allowed kdamond to continue operating on a damon_ctx after damon_commit_ctx() failed, even though that function can leave the destination context partially updated and only safe for destruction.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that on damon_commit_ctx() failure “the damon_ctx ... can be partially updated (or, corrupted from a perspective), and therefore shouldn't be used anymore,” yet “DAMON may run with the partially updated damon_ctx”; the patch adds a new damon_ctx->maybe_corrupted flag set to true at the start of damon_commit_ctx(), cleared only on success, and checked in kdamond_call(), kdamond_wait_activation(), and kdamond_fn() to stop further use of the context.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The DAMON core allowed kdamond to continue operating on a damon_ctx after damon_commit_ctx() failed, even though that function can leave the destination context partially updated and only safe for destruction.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that on damon_commit_ctx() failure “the damon_ctx ... can be partially updated (or, corrupted from a perspective), and therefore shouldn't be used anymore,” yet “DAMON may run with the partially updated damon_ctx”; the patch adds a new damon_ctx->maybe_corrupted flag set to true at the start of damon_commit_ctx(), cleared only on success, and checked in kdamond_call(), kdamond_wait_activation(), and kdamond_fn() to stop further use of the context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a corruption-state flag to damon_ctx so commit failures can mark the context as potentially invalid.
intent_record.what: A new boolean field named maybe_corrupted was added to struct damon_ctx, along with a comment stating that it indicates the context may be corrupted and is currently set only on damon_commit_ctx() failure.
intent_record.how: This change extends the DAMON context structure with state to record a possible corruption condition, enabling runtime code to mark and later inspect whether a context may be invalid after a commit failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark the destination context as potentially corrupted at the start of commit so failed or partial updates are not treated as clean state.
intent_record.what: A single assignment was added at the start of damon_commit_ctx(): `dst->maybe_corrupted = true;` before the existing validation of `src->min_region_sz`.
intent_record.how: This marks the destination DAMON context as potentially corrupted as soon as a commit begins, including cases where the function later exits early due to invalid input, so runtime logic can treat the partially updated destination state as unsafe or needing recovery.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the destination context's corruption flag on successful commit so stale corrupted state is not carried over.
intent_record.what: A new assignment was added in damon_commit_ctx() to explicitly set dst->maybe_corrupted = false before returning success.
intent_record.how: When committing a DAMON context from src to dst, the destination context now has its maybe_corrupted flag cleared, preventing it from retaining a previous corrupted-state indication after a successful commit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop further non-cancel call-control processing when the DAMON context may be corrupted.
intent_record.what: A new conditional was added inside the loop in kdamond_call(): after handling completion or freeing a canceled control, the code now checks `if (!cancel && ctx->maybe_corrupted)` and executes `break;` when true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, during normal (non-cancel) processing, the loop will now stop iterating further if the context is marked as maybe corrupted, preventing additional call controls from being processed once corruption is detected.

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort kdamond activation waiting with -EINVAL when the DAMON context is marked maybe_corrupted to avoid continuing on a potentially corrupted state.
intent_record.what: In kdamond_wait_activation(), after the call to kdamond_call(ctx, false), a new conditional was added to check ctx->maybe_corrupted and immediately return -EINVAL if it is true, before calling damos_walk_cancel(ctx).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes the activation wait path to abort early with an invalid-argument style error when the context has been marked as potentially corrupted, instead of continuing normal processing and cancellation handling. This prevents further operation on a possibly corrupted DAMON context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop kdamond processing when the context may be corrupted to avoid executing further operations on invalid state.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added immediately after kdamond_call(ctx, false); in kdamond_fn(): if (ctx->maybe_corrupted) break;.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the loop in kdamond_fn() now exits early when the context is marked maybe_corrupted, preventing subsequent scheme processing or other loop work from running on a potentially corrupted context state.

grouping_result.intent: Clear the destination context's corruption flag on successful commit so stale corrupted state is not carried over.
Stop kdamond processing when the context may be corrupted to avoid executing further operations on invalid state.

consistency_review.core_intent: Track and manage a DAMON context corruption flag across commit operations so failed or partial updates mark the destination as potentially invalid and successful commits clear that state.
Add defensive guards to stop or abort kdamond/DAMON processing when the context is marked maybe_corrupted, preventing further operations on invalid state.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause by marking a DAMON context as potentially corrupted during commit, preserving that state on failure/partial update, and clearing it only on success. This addresses the unsafe continued use of a partially updated damon_ctx after damon_commit_ctx() fails.

The changes directly prevent kdamond/DAMON from continuing to operate on a context marked maybe_corrupted, which matches the root cause of continuing execution after damon_commit_ctx() failure leaves the context only safe for destruction.

candidates.rationale: The commit function had no preexisting mechanism in this hunk to mark the destination context unsafe during update and only returned success/failure. This allowed callers to keep using dst after a failed/partial commit because no corrupted-state tracking was established.
kdamond continued invoking normal processing on the context without checking whether a prior damon_commit_ctx() failure had left ctx partially updated and unsafe to use.
This processing path likewise continued operating on ctx with no guard for a failed/partial commit, directly matching the root cause of using a potentially corrupted DAMON context.

Subsequent DAMON operations proceeded on ctx unconditionally after commit-related state changes, despite the possibility that the context had been left partially updated and was only safe for destruction.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement continues normal kdamond processing on ctx without checking whether a prior damon_commit_ctx() failure left the context partially updated and only safe for destruction, directly matching the root cause.
This statement gates further DAMON operations on ctx without any corruption-state check, allowing use of a context that may have been left partially updated after damon_commit_ctx() failed.

Within damon_commit_ctx(), this success-path statement existed without any prior marking of the destination context as potentially corrupted during update, so callers had no state indicating that a failed or partial commit could leave the context unsafe to continue using.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `damon_commit_ctx()` and its helper commit functions, which is enough to judge the root cause. The vulnerability root cause is that `damon_commit_ctx()` can fail after partially modifying `dst`, leaving it only safe for destruction, yet callers may continue using it. This implementation clearly has that property. In `damon_commit_ctx()`, it first does `err = damon_commit_schemes(dst, src); if (err) return err;`, then `err = damon_commit_targets(dst, src); if (err) return err;`, then `err = damon_set_attrs(dst, &src->attrs); if (err) return err;`, and finally `dst->ops = src->ops;`. There is no rollback or marking of `dst` as unusable on failure. The helpers also mutate `dst` incrementally before returning errors: for example, `damos_commit()` assigns multiple fields (`dst->pattern = src->pattern;`, `dst->action = src->action;`, `dst->apply_interval_us = src->apply_interval_us;`) before later operations can fail; `damos_commit_filters()` may destroy existing filters and then return `-ENOMEM` while adding new ones; `damon_commit_schemes()` may update or destroy existing schemes and then fail creating a new one; `damon_commit_targets()` may update/destroy targets and then fail; `damon_commit_target()` updates regions and pid state in place. Therefore this commit introduces the vulnerable construct: `damon_commit_ctx()` can return an error after partially updating the destination context. The fix described in the root cause—preventing continued operation on such a partially updated context—is not present in this function.
